sentences.text: Myriacanthus was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish in the order Chimaeriformes.
This animal possessed an elongated snout and a head protected by armor plates with spines extending backward from the jaw corners.
A fused cartilage block called a synarcual supported the dorsal fin, while rings formed the spinal column behind the head.
Based on the head and neck size, the total length of Myriacanthus was likely over 1 meter.
The genus was first named by Louis Agassiz in 1836 based on a fin spine found in Jurassic rocks at Lyme Regis, Dorset.
The specimen used for the genus was previously identified by Henry De la Beche in 1822.
Myriacanthus belongs to the family Myriacanthidae and the order Chimaeriformes, serving as the type genus of that family.
Myriacanthus lived from the Rhaetian to the Sinemurian, between 205.7 and 192.9 million years ago.
